senses.gloss:
Āmra
inscriptional poet, son of Ādityanāga an. pupil of Vedāṅgamuni, who silenced Buddhists an. Jains; ins. dated 971 A. D. JBBRAS. XXII. 1908, p.. 152, 167. [Page149-a.

Āmradeva
of Dhārā, father of Narapati who wrote in A. D. 1176 his Narapatijayacaryā a. Anahilapaṭṭaṇa, under Ajayapāla (1174-77 A. D.). BBRAS. 381. Bik. 691. IO. 3109. Lz. 1160. Weber 1744.

Āmradeva
a. ancestor of the commander Āhlādana (Saṁ. 1299), patron of Vardhamāna (Vāsupūjyacarita). BBRAS. 1772.

Āmradeva
pupil of Uddyotana sūri of Bṛhatgaccha an. teacher of Nemicandra (Ākhyānamaṇikośa etc.). BBRAS. 1639.

Āmradeva
(ammadeva Pkt.) guru of Nemicandra (Pravacanasāroddhāra) an. pupil of Jinabhadra (or Jinacandra) sūri. BBRAS. 1639. Peters. I. Intro. p. 69. Weber 1936-39.

Āmradeva
(or amra or amaradeva) Jain. guru of Nemicandra (Anantanātha caritra Pūjāṣṭaka). Pattan Intro. p. 69. Same a. the previous ?

Āmradeva
pupil or grandpupil of Nemicandra; wrote under King Jayasiṁha of Dhavalakka in 1134 A. D.
--C. on Ākhyānamaṇikośa of Nemicandra. See above under Ākhyānaº. See also Praśasti I. p. 26.

Āmradeva
Jain. of the Pūrṇatalliyagaccha. Ref. to in the C. on Mūlaśuddhiprakaraṇa of Pradyumnasūri. Peters. V. p. 165.

Āmradevācārya_(?)
--C. Cūrṇi on Pañcakalpasūtra. BORI. 162 of 1873-74. D. p. 62. Kh. 162.

Āmrāvatīmāhātmya
paur. Oppert II. 2220. 2317. 2421. 2589. Same a. next ?

Āmrāvatī(garbhapurī)māhātmya
paur. from the Brahmakaivartapurāṇa, on Karur, Tiruchi D.. Trav. Uni. 3580C (chs. 108-116).
